title: Newton's law of gravitation
examples: How does the distance between two objects change the gravitational force?
What is the formula for the gravitational force between two masses?
Can you explain what the 'inverse square' part means in this law?

explain.say: Today we look at the force between two masses.
The force is directly proportional to the product of the two masses.
The force is inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.
The constant G is the universal gravitational constant.
Consider the Earth and the Moon orbiting each other.
If you double the distance between two masses, the force becomes four times smaller.

faq.q: What does the 'inverse square' really mean?
faq.a: It means that if you change the distance by a certain factor, the force changes by the square of that factor. For example, doubling the distance reduces the force to one-fourth of its original strength.
asks: How does distance affect the force?
What is the mathematical relationship with distance?

faq.q: Do we need to use the constant G every time?
faq.a: Yes, the constant G must be included in the calculation unless you are comparing forces on the same two objects. It is essential for getting the correct numerical answer.
asks: Is G always needed in the formula?
What is the role of the constant G?

faq.q: Does the force depend on the objects' shapes?
faq.a: No, Newton's law assumes the objects are point masses. Therefore, the shape does not affect the calculated gravitational force between their centers.
asks: Does the shape matter for gravity?
Is this law only for perfect spheres?

faq.q: Can this law explain why we stay on Earth?
faq.a: Yes, the force keeping us on Earth is the gravitational attraction between our mass and the Earth's mass. This force is what we call weight.
asks: Why is gravity keeping me grounded?
How does this law relate to weight?

faq.q: If I use kilograms for mass and meters for distance, what are the units of force?
faq.a: The resulting unit for the force will be Newtons, which is the standard unit for force in the International System of Units.
asks: What are the units for the force?
What units should I get for the answer?

facts: The law states that the force is proportional to the product of the masses.
The force is inversely proportional to the square of the distance.
The constant G is approximately 6.67 times ten to the power of negative eleven.
The force always acts along the line connecting the centers of the two masses.

quiz.say: If the distance between two masses is tripled, the new force will be:

options.show: the same as the original force
options.say: the same as the original force

quiz.why: Because the force is inversely proportional to the square of the distance, tripling the distance means the force is divided by three squared, which is nine.

wrong.0: This incorrectly assumes the force increases with distance.
wrong.1: This ignores the dependence on the separation distance.
wrong.3: This confuses the inverse square law with a simple inverse relationship.

quiz.say: Which quantity is directly proportional to the gravitational force?

options.show: the product of the two masses
options.say: the product of the two masses

options.show: the sum of the two masses
options.say: the sum of the two masses

quiz.why: The formula shows that if you increase either mass, the force increases proportionally.

wrong.0: The force is inversely proportional to the square of the distance.
wrong.1: The relationship is inverse, not direct, with distance.
wrong.3: The law uses the product, not the sum, of the masses.

quiz.say: If you calculate the force between two objects and use incorrect units for G, what will happen?

options.show: the force will be calculated correctly
options.say: the force will be calculated correctly

options.show: your final answer will have incorrect units
options.say: your final answer will have incorrect units

quiz.why: The units of G are crucial because they define the units for the resulting force calculation.

wrong.0: Only zero mass or infinite distance would result in zero force.
wrong.1: Using wrong units for a constant will always lead to a wrong result.
wrong.2: The units of G affect the final force unit, not the input mass units.
